speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this persistent cough and shortness of breath, and does it worsen at night or with exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: It's been going on for about two weeks now. The cough and breathlessness definitely get worse when I'm working hard or when I lie down to sleep at night. However, the payer has pre-authorization restrictions on endocrine lab panels. No tests can be ordered today. Proceed with clinical diagnosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the restrictions, so let's focus on your symptoms. Does the shortness of breath come on suddenly or build up gradually, and have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles?

speaker: Patient
text: The shortness of breath usually builds up gradually, especially when I'm exerting myself, and I haven't noticed any swelling in my legs or ankles. I do, however, hear a whistling sound in my chest occasionally when I breathe out. I want to emphasize that, the payer has pre-authorization restrictions on endocrine lab panels. No tests can be ordered today. Proceed with clinical diagnosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: That whistling sound is very important; does it happen only when you exhale, and do you have a history of smoking or exposure to dust and chemicals? Also, have you experienced any wheezing episodes in the past that resolved with an inhaler?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, the whistling sound only happens when I breathe out. I have never smoked, but I work as a construction worker and am frequently exposed to dust. I did have similar episodes last year that were treated with inhalers.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Occupational Asthma (likely due to construction dust exposure).
